items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: I heard Zellie too. ... I'm pretty sure I heard him at Hilma Burke's one night as I was passing by.

ctx.x: Listen, Jerry plays, sings like him, he sings high pitched.

There's a couple of spots when Jerry recorded that, the homers in a southern town, I don't know if you ever heard of him recording, but there are a couple of spots there that he reminded me of jazz, a little bit like Tony. It's one of my favorite Jerry Roll records. Is it? Yeah, he reminds me a little. It's a wonder he didn't get to singing more earlier. How did, how did you ever get to going down in the district to hear those guys playing? Well, it just, just like I told you, that one night I was just, they had…
Well then the New Orleans Blues was written in 1906, wasn't it? Well he, yes.
